indicator.1: Desktop without GNOME (or gnome-extensions tool missing): the indicator only exists for GNOME for now.
indicator.2: Indicator missing ({gnome_extension_dir}): install version 0.49.0 or later (menu 7.3).
indicator.3:
The indicator is installed but GNOME does not know it yet: log out and log back in,
then come back to this menu.
indicator.4:
The indicator shows at the top of the screen, left of the sound icon: a light (green receive, red transmit,
orange alert, grey station stopped, purple safety lockout), the frequency or the transmission countdown,
and on click the full status (clients, transceiver, spectrum, DX Cluster, temperature, update...).
It only READS the station status: it cannot control anything.
State: {v}.
indicator.11: Indicator enabled: it appears at the top right.
indicator.12: Enabling failed (code {code}): log out, log back in and try again.
hwtest.2: Before the test, check the computer's sound:
hwtest.3:
Test on the real transceiver:
  1) receive only (no transmission): CAT, received audio, tuning, filter widths, spectrum scope
  2) full: the same, then transmission (dummy load, reduced power, confirmation at each step)
qualif.2:
Transceiver qualification (trx-qualif), for an expert:
  1) test plan and Hamlib inconsistencies, without touching the transceiver
  2) exploration WITHOUT transmission: everything Hamlib declares is read and compared with the transceiver
     (frequency and a few receive settings changed, then put back)
  3) read-only exploration: nothing is changed on the transceiver
  4) qualification without transmission (verdict "incomplete": the transmission phase is not done)
  5) full qualification, with transmission (dummy load, reduced power, confirmation at each step)
  6) ON-SITE qualification kit: before / after snapshots, exploration, qualification, timed safety drills,
     zip report for Claude (the kit stops and starts the station itself)
Reports: {path}
start.2: Station started. A diagnostic is advised in a few seconds (menu 6.1).
stop.1: Station stopped (the transceiver stays in receive).
report.2:
Report created: {path}
It contains no password: attach it to your request for help.
clear_safe_mode.1:
The supervisor put the station into safety lockout after repeated failures.
Check the cause first (menu 6.1 and menu 6.2).
clear_safe_mode.2: The cause is fixed, reactivate the station

menu.monitoring: Station-to-station monitoring (help an operator in trouble, or get help)
monitoring.off:
Monitoring disabled, or "monlink" module never started.
To enable it: menu {menu} "Features in service", line "Monitoring between stations" (sets [monitor_link] and [modules] run),
then restart the station (menu {start}).
monitoring.menu:
1) Choose the nickname
  2) Links and latest news
  3) Help someone: create an invitation code
  4) Get help: join with a code
  5) Compare the fingerprint of a pending link
  6) Ask for assistance mode or the troubleshooting report (helping station)
  7) Answer a request (helped station)
  8) What is sent, pause, resume (helped station)
  9) End a link
 10) Troubleshooting report: send mine (helped station), or copy the received one to the Desktop (helping station)
Choice (Enter = back):
monitoring.summary.head: Monitoring: nickname {pseudo}, {reg}
monitoring.summary.none: No link: help someone (choice 3) or get help (choice 4).
monitoring.do.noreply: No answer from the "monlink" module (station stopped? see the log, menu {menu}).
monitoring.pseudo.ask: Nickname (1 to 16 characters: unaccented letters, digits, space . / _ -):
monitoring.view.head: {pseudo} ({role}, {state})
monitoring.view.profile: You send: events from "{min}" up, every {period} min; frequency and mode {fm}
monitoring.invite.done:
Code to read out to the operator you help: {code}
Valid for 15 minutes, once only. When they have typed it (menu {menu}, choice 4), come back to choice 5 to compare the 6 digits.
monitoring.join.intro: Get help: the helping station will receive what YOU choose (computer health, rig state, error codes), always masked (passwords, addresses, serial numbers). It can command NOTHING. You can stop everything at any time (menu {menu}, choice 9).
monitoring.join.ask: Code read out by the person helping you (10 characters):
monitoring.fp.show:
Fingerprint: {fp}
Compare these 6 digits with your contact's, by voice or by message.
monitoring.fp.same: Does your contact see exactly the same 6 digits?
monitoring.fp.differ: Digits different or not confirmed: link refused and deleted. Start again with a new code.
monitoring.profile.menu:
What you send:
  1) Essential: computer health and errors
  2) Diagnostic: also rig state and warnings (recommended)
monitoring.profile.fm: Also send the rig frequency and mode?
monitoring.request.menu:
Duration of the assistance mode requested:
  1) 1 hour
  2) 2 hours
  3) 4 hours
  4) 24 hours
monitoring.request.done: Request sent: the helped operator must accept it (menu {menu}, choice 7).
monitoring.answer.show: {pseudo} asks for assistance mode for {hours} h: news every 30 seconds and all events, even informational ones. Frequency and mode stay as you chose.
monitoring.answer.yes: Assistance accepted for {hours} h; it stops by itself afterwards.
monitoring.answer.no: Request refused; your contact is told.
monitoring.manage.menu:
1) Change what is sent
  2) Pause
  3) Resume sending
monitoring.end.ask: End the link with {pseudo}? Immediate; resuming it will need a new code.
monitoring.end.purge: Also delete what was received from this station?
monitoring.request.kind:
Ask for:
  1) assistance mode (news every 30 seconds)
  2) the troubleshooting report (the one of menu 6.3, masked)
monitoring.answer.report_show: {pseudo} asks for your troubleshooting report (the one of menu 6.3: diagnostics, configuration without passwords, logs), fully masked before sending (computer name, addresses, accounts, serial numbers).
monitoring.report.queued: Report being prepared: it leaves within the next minute (a few seconds to build).
monitoring.report.copy_failed: Copy failed ({exc}); the report is here: {path}

local_operator.1: Operator on site: someone transmits with the transceiver microphone, in front of it. The station never starts a transmission; the supervisor can only cut.
local_operator.state: Shared station: {shared}; absolute TOT: {abs} s; local transmission allowed when the operator is present: {present} s
local_operator.2: Shared station (a transmission with the transceiver microphone is only cut by the absolute TOT, or later when the operator is present)
local_operator.3: Supervisor absolute TOT, in seconds (cuts ANY transmission beyond it)
local_operator.4: Local transmission allowed when the operator is present (touched the transceiver), in seconds
alerts.menu:
1) ntfy address (e.g. https://ntfy.sh/a-long-secret-topic)
  2) Alert language (fr or en)
  3) "Station in service" message (every N hours)
  4) Send a test alert now
Choice (Enter = back):
alerts.url: New address (https://…, "-" = no more alerts, Enter = unchanged):
alerts.url_bad: Refused: the address must start with https:// (or http://), without spaces.
alerts.alive: Every how many hours (0 = none, 0.25 to 168; Enter = {alive}):
alerts.none_to_test: No address: choose it first (choice 1) and save it.
alerts.test_sent: Test alert sent (ORT-8025): look at the phone. Nothing received? Check the topic subscription in the ntfy app.
alerts.test_failed: Sending failed: {exc}. Check the address and the station Internet access.
features.title: Station features (the number toggles IN SERVICE / OFF; the station restarts to apply it):
indicator.win.state: Indicator next to the clock (read only). Started at each session logon: {v}.
indicator.win.menu:
1) Start the indicator now
  2) Start it or not at each session logon (toggle)
Choice (Enter = back):
indicator.win.started: Indicator started: if it is hidden under "^", drag it next to the clock.
indicator.win.failed: Cannot start it (pythonw.exe missing?): reinstall the station.
indicator.win.on: The indicator will start at each session logon.
indicator.win.off: The indicator will no longer start at session logon.
updates.store: Microsoft Store version {installed}: updates come through the Microsoft Store (openRemoteTRX page: {link}). Stop the station (menu 1.2) before starting the update, radio in receive: the configuration is kept. No going back to a previous version.
store.zip_installed: The zip version of the station is installed on this PC (scheduled task "openRemoteTRX"): the Microsoft Store station does not start (ORT-8029). Uninstall the zip version from Settings > Apps > openRemoteTRX; your configuration is kept.
updates.windows: On Windows, a new version is installed by running installer.cmd from the new zip (project releases page): the configuration is kept. Rolling back: run installer.cmd from the older version again.
tui.hint: Digit: theme then menu (0 = language) · ↑↓ Enter · mouse: hover = help, click = choose, 2nd click = open · + / -: expand / collapse all · r or Esc: back · q: quit
monitor.new_window: Dashboard opened in a new tab or window; openRemoteTRX Console stays here.
monitor.tmux_tip: (SSH connection: the dashboard opens here. Tip: start openRemoteTRX Console inside tmux, it will then open in another tmux window.)
web.title: openRemoteTRX Console
web.search: Search a setting: ntfy, TOT, visitor, certificate…
web.busy: A menu is running in the terminal: finish it first (or answer its question).
web.webapp_open: Open the station's control page in a new tab
tui.web_started: Web console started: it opens in the browser.
tui.web_ssh: SSH connection: run "trx-console --web" on the station, then the SSH tunnel it shows (guide, part 7).
remote_console.1: openRemoteTRX Console on the network: the same menus in the browser of any PC, tablet or phone on the local network or VPN, without SSH. Login with an ADMINISTRATOR operator account; session closed after 30 minutes without action; the station sudo password is still asked once per session. Never reachable from the Internet.
remote_console.state: In service: {on}; HTTPS port: {port}; administrator accounts: {admins}
remote_console.2: Put openRemoteTRX Console on the network in service
remote_console.done:
openRemoteTRX Console can be reached from the network: {urls}
An administrator operator logged in to the control page also finds the link there (“openRemoteTRX Console” section, under “Connexion”).
remote_console.no_operator: No operator account with a password: create one first (menu {menu}).
remote_console.admins: Numbers of the ADMINISTRATOR accounts, separated by spaces (Enter = keep the marked ones):
remote_console.admins_bad: Answer refused: type numbers from the list (e.g. 1 3).
remote_console.admins_none: At least one administrator account is needed, otherwise nobody could log in.
remote_console.account: Linux account running the console, the one you administer with [{current}]:
remote_console.account_bad: “{user}” refused: a Linux account name (lowercase, digits, _ . -), never root.
remote_console.no_tls: Warning: the station has no HTTPS certificate. Do menu {menu} first, otherwise the console will not start.
remote_console.local_only: Warning: the station page only listens on this machine (127.0.0.1). To open it from the network: menu {menu}.
remote_console.stopped: openRemoteTRX Console on the network is stopped.
remote_console.service_failed: The trx-console-web@{account} service did not start: see “journalctl -u trx-console-web@{account}” (menu 6.2).
web.login.title: openRemoteTRX Console login
web.login.bad: Refused: wrong login or password, or account without administration right.
web.login.blocked: Too many attempts: try again in {minutes} min.
web.login.note: Your station operator account (marked administrator in menu 4.6). Session closed after a while without action.
level.title: Display level (current: {level}): it hides menus to keep things simple, without forbidding anything.
level.basic.desc: commissioning, daily use, asking for help
level.expert.desc: plus fine settings and development tools
level.hidden_menu: Menu {key} ({level} level): hidden at the chosen level, opened anyway.
web.sudo_refused: Administration password refused: command not run.
web.flow.sudo: Station administration password (sudo): asked once per session, never stored.
web.flow.busy: A menu is already open: finish or stop it first.
web.dash.stale: Gateway frozen or absent: values are no longer up to date.
web.edit.hint: Edit the text, then “Check and save”: the station checks everything and shows the differences before writing; nothing is written if it is wrong.
features.diffusion: Live broadcast to an Icecast server
diffusion.menu:
1) Start a broadcast   2) Stop the broadcast   3) Show the listeners' username and password
4) New listeners' password   5) Server settings   6) Server secrets (source password, key)
Choice (Enter = back):
diffusion.no_module: No news from the "diffusion" module: feature not switched on yet (menu {menu}) or station stopped (menu {start}). Server settings (5) and secrets (6) can still be set here.
diffusion.off: Broadcast switched off: switch it on in menu {menu} (after setting the server: choices 5 and 6).
diffusion.live: ON AIR: {access} channel, started by {operator}, {left} left, listeners: {listeners}, transmitted voice broadcast: {voice}.
diffusion.cause.auth: source password refused by the server
diffusion.bands_on: Outside the allowed bands: everything is broadcast.
diffusion.bands_off: Outside the allowed bands: silence for the listeners (the broadcast goes on).
diffusion.silence: Right now, SILENCE for the listeners: {v}.
diffusion.silence.pas_de_son: the rig audio no longer reaches the module
diffusion.noreply: The "diffusion" module does not answer: station stopped or feature switched off (log: menu {menu}).
diffusion.access_list:
1) Private: listeners are asked for a username and password (advised)
  2) Public: plain address, no password
diffusion.ask_voice: Also broadcast your voice while you transmit
diffusion.warning: WARNING: you are about to rebroadcast the audio of your TRX on the Internet, to listeners without an account on the station. What you broadcast is YOUR responsibility. Outside the allowed bands listeners hear nothing unless the "outside bands" setting is on; while you transmit, your voice is broadcast only if you asked for it.
diffusion.confirm: Start anyway (asked only once for this station)
diffusion.started: Broadcast started. Address to give your listeners: {url}
diffusion.no_password: none yet (generated at the first private start)
diffusion.ask_generate: Generate a new password for the listeners? The old one will stop working (those already listening are not cut off)
diffusion.new_password: New listeners' password, to pass on to them:
diffusion.settings_state: Server: {server}; station: {station}; codec: {codec}; source port: {port}; broadcast outside bands: {bands}
diffusion.settings_menu:
1) Server   2) Station name   3) Codec   4) Outside the allowed bands   5) Source port
Choice (Enter = back):
diffusion.ask_server: Name of the broadcast server, given by its administrator (e.g. diffusion.example.org):
diffusion.ask_station: Station name on this server (2 to 32 characters a-z, 0-9, -):
diffusion.ask_codec: Codec: opus (light, advised) or mp3 (old iPhones, radio apps) [{codec}]:
diffusion.bands_explain: You decide what is broadcast. No: silence for the listeners when the rig leaves the allowed bands of station.toml (the broadcast goes on, the audio comes back inside a band). Yes: everything is broadcast.
diffusion.ask_bands: Also broadcast outside the allowed bands
diffusion.ask_port: Source port (given by the server administrator)
diffusion.secrets_explain: The source password and the metadata key are given by the server administrator. They are saved in diffusion.key (readable by the service only), never in station.toml, never shown.
diffusion.secrets_saved: Secrets saved in {file}. Used from the next broadcast start.
diffusion.secrets_listener_note: The listeners' password could not be read back (module stopped?): a new one will be generated at the next private start.
remote_power.1: Remote power on and off: an operator who connects switches the radio on if it is off; STOP held 3 s in the page or the app switches it off (with confirmation). Off by default. The station never transmits to switch the radio on or off.
remote_power.state: On: {on}; automatic switch-off: {idle} (after {hours} h without connection); ntfy alerts: {notify}; port USB identity: {ident}
remote_power.2: Switch remote power on and off on
remote_power.unsupported: According to Hamlib, your radio cannot be switched on or off over CAT: feature left off.
remote_power.caps_unknown: Cannot read what Hamlib declares for this radio (rigctl not found?): feature left off.
remote_power.warning: WARNING: a radio switched off remotely only comes back on over CAT. If your radio cuts its USB once off, you will have to press ON/OFF at the shack. Yaesu: USB socket only, not the RS-232C socket.
remote_power.trial_ask: Run the trial now (station stopped during the trial, radio switched off then on, no transmission)
remote_power.trial_failed: Trial failed: remote power stays off.
remote_power.3: Automatic switch-off after a delay without any connection
remote_power.4: Delay without connection before switch-off, in hours
remote_power.5: ntfy alert at each switch-on, switch-off or failure
remote_power.no_ntfy: ntfy alerts not configured: set them up in menu {menu}.
rx_gain.1: Receive audio gain: level of the rig audio sent to every terminal (phones, page, visitors, broadcast). The receive limiter caps peaks at -1 dBFS: a high gain does not clip. The volume of each phone is set in the page or the app.
rx_gain.level: Level received right now: {level} dBFS (target: {target} dBFS on a voice or band noise); suggested gain: {suggest} dB
rx_gain.limited: The limiter lowered the audio {pct} % of the time since the station started.
rx_gain.no_level: Received level unknown (station stopped or rig silent): start the station, tune the rig to a frequency with signal, then come back to this menu for a suggested value.
rx_gain.warning: WARNING: limiter off, a positive gain or a strong signal may clip (distorted audio). Keep it for troubleshooting only.
